{{short description|Numerical computation of special functions}}
{{about|reflection in number theory and calculus|reflection formulas in geometry|Reflection (mathematics)}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''reflection formula''' or '''reflection relation''' for a [[function (mathematics)|function]] {{mvar|f}} is a relationship between {{math|''f''(''a'' − ''x'')}} and {{math|''f''(''x'')}}.  It is a special case of a [[functional equation]]. It is common in mathematical literature to use the term "functional equation" for what are specifically reflection formulae.

Reflection formulae are useful for [[numerical analysis|numerical computation]] of [[special function]]s. In effect, an approximation that has greater accuracy or only converges on one side of a reflection point (typically in the positive half of the [[complex plane]]) can be employed for all arguments.

== Known formulae ==
The [[even and odd functions]] satisfy by definition simple reflection relations around {{math|1=''a'' = 0}}. For all even functions,

<math display=block>f(-x) = f(x),</math>

and for all odd functions,

<math display=block>f(-x) = -f(x).</math>

A famous relationship is '''Euler's reflection formula'''

<math display=block>\Gamma(z)\Gamma(1-z) = \frac{\pi}{\sin{(\pi z)}}, \qquad z \not\in \mathbb Z</math>

for the [[gamma function]] <math display=inline>\Gamma(z)</math>, due to [[Leonhard Euler]].

There is also a reflection formula for the general {{mvar|n}}-th order [[polygamma function]] {{math|''ψ''{{sup|(''n'')}}(''z'')}},

<math display=block>\psi^{(n)} (1-z)+(-1)^{n+1}\psi^{(n)} (z) = (-1)^n \pi \frac{d^n}{d z^n} \cot{(\pi z)} </math>

which springs trivially from the fact that the polygamma functions are defined as the derivatives of <math display=inline>\ln \Gamma</math> and thus inherit the reflection formula.

The [[dilogarithm]] also satisfies a reflection formula,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Dilogarithm |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Dilogarithm.html |access-date=2025-09-01 |website=Wolfram MathWorld |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dilogarithm Reflection Formula - ProofWiki |url=https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Dilogarithm_Reflection_Formula |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=proofwiki.org}}</ref>

<math display=block>\operatorname{Li}_2(z)+\operatorname{Li}_2(1-z)=\zeta(2)-\ln (z)\ln(1-z)</math>

The [[Riemann zeta function]] {{math|''ζ''(''z'')}} satisfies

<math display=block>\frac{\zeta(1-z)}{\zeta(z)} = \frac{2\, \Gamma(z)}{(2\pi)^{z}} \cos\left(\frac{\pi z}{2}\right),</math>

and the [[Riemann Xi function]] {{math|''ξ''(''z'')}} satisfies

<math display=block>\xi(z) = \xi(1-z). </math>
